title: From Geographic Memory to Spatial Generalization in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.25703v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can associate places with geographic descriptions, but recovering an observed association does not establish an ability to generalize across geographic space. We distinguish geospatial memory, the recovery of location--description associations observed during training, from spatial generalization, the prediction of descriptions for locations in unobserved regions. We investigate whether continuous location representations improve this generalization and encourage geographic knowledge to become spatially organized within an LLM. We frame this organization as a latent spatial field: a learned mapping from locations to descriptions connected through spatial dependencies. Building on a continuous spatial encoder, we project location representations into the model's embedding space and supply them as spatial tokens. We evaluate the resulting models on two newly curated geo-text benchmarks for Los Angeles and Lon

translated_title: 从地理记忆到大语言模型中的空间泛化
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）能够将地点与地理描述相关联，但恢复训练中观察到的关联并不能证明其具备跨地理空间泛化的能力。我们区分了“地理空间记忆”（即恢复训练期间观察到的位置—描述关联）与“空间泛化”（即为未观察区域中的位置预测描述）。我们研究连续的位置表示能否改善这种泛化能力，并促使地理知识在大语言模型内部形成空间化的组织。我们将这种组织形式构建为一个潜在空间场：一种通过空间依赖关系连接的、从位置到描述的学习映射。基于连续空间编码器，我们将位置表示投影到模型的嵌入空间中，并将其作为空间标记提供。我们在两个新构建的地理文本基准（分别针对洛杉矶和伦敦）上评估了所得模型。
tldr: 该论文提出将大语言模型中的地理知识组织为潜在空间场，通过连续空间编码器将位置表示作为空间标记注入模型，从而实现从仅能回忆训练中见过的“地理空间记忆”向能预测未见区域的“空间泛化”能力的跨越。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes organizing geographic knowledge in LLMs as a latent spatial field by injecting continuous location representations as spatial tokens, enabling models to move beyond mere "geospatial memory" of observed associations toward true "spatial generalization" to unobserved regions.
